amendments.because: An earlier owner-facing output fix set titles to at most 70 characters; only the cut at the first comma was wrong
amendments.done_when: A pull request's title is the whole first sentence of the item's why, shortened at a word boundary only when it passes GitHub's title length

done_when: A pull request's title is the first sentence of the item's why, never cut at a comma or inside a version number, and shortened at a word boundary to at most 70 characters

findings.body: Raise: Not done. A fix why such as `The command prints "Failed." Retry it.` produces a title containing both sentences: the expression on line 963 does not recognize sentence-ending punctuation followed by a closing quote. Line 965 also fails the 70-character limit when the first word is longer than 71 characters: `rfind` returns -1, so the slice removes only the final character. The named command tests use unquoted sentence endings and have spaces before character 70, so they pass in both cases.
findings.title: Not done: PR titles can include a second sentence or exceed 70 characters

why: Pull request titles stop at the first comma of the fix's why, so titles read 'On Windows' or 'Clients and this repo need v1'
